target: Independent method reproduction of section 5.6 / table 5.7; not original author checkpoints

training.population: four independent networks of the same kind, all learn once after each full game
training.selection: final checkpoint, fixed agent index 0; never select using evaluation results

primaryEvaluation.metric: dirv minus alpha fractional first-place win share, in percentage points
primaryEvaluation.interval: 95% paired percentile bootstrap over independent deal groups; 10000 resamples

secondaryEvaluation.purpose: predeclared independent replication without parameter changes

timeMatchedEvaluation.checkpointSelection: After Alpha completes 2000 games, capture the current completed DirV checkpoint without inspecting win rates; verify training elapsed times differ by at most 5%
timeMatchedEvaluation.purpose: Additional predeclared comparison at approximately equal measured training time; separately verify decision time ratio

interpretation: Report whether the primary interval excludes zero; do not stop early for significance.
Report both training elapsed time and decision mean/p95; the paper's simulation ratio need not give equal time on this implementation.
A count-matched result is not a time-matched claim when timing differs materially.
The paper's 40% vs 29% is a reference observation, not an optimization target.
A single pair of training seeds does not establish stability across training initializations.
